subject: general
question: Which type of line is used to represent hidden edges or surfaces in a technical drawing, as per BIS SP 46-2003?
solution:
The correct answer is __Dashed thin line.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Dashed thin lines__ are used in technical drawings to represent hidden edges or surfaces.
 
• This type of line is specified in technical drawing standards such as BIS SP 46-2003.
 
• It helps in understanding the internal features or surfaces of an object that are not visible from the outside.
 
• Dashed thin lines are uniformly spaced and consistent in their appearance throughout the drawing.
 
• They play a crucial role in clearly communicating design intent to engineers, manufacturers, and other stakeholders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Continuous thick line:**

 
 
• Used to represent visible edges and outlines of an object in technical drawings.
 
• It is the most prominent line in the drawing and provides the main structure of the object.
 
 
 
• **Chain thin line:**
 
 
• Used to represent centerlines or axes of symmetry in a drawing.
 
• It is characterized by alternating short and long dashes.
 
 
 
• **Continuous thin line:**
 
 
• Used for dimensions, extension lines, and other annotations in a technical drawing.
 
• It is less prominent than thick lines and serves as supplementary information.
